graph.title: 8x8 LED Matrix Row-Column Scanning
notes: Fix for E12: all 8 x 1k resistors are now on the matrix columns (C1-C8), one per column; the 8 rows (R1-R8) go straight to the Arduino with green wires. In the manual's image the resistors sit on Arduino pins 2-9, which are a mix of rows and columns, so I moved them to the column side as the spec requires.

The Arduino pin for every matrix pin is unchanged and follows the manual's pin table (matrix pin 1=R5->13, 2=R7->12, 3=C2->11, 4=C3->10, 5=R8->A2, 6=C5->A3, 7=R6->A4, 8=R3->A5, 9=R1->2, 10=C4->3, 11=C6->4, 12=R4->5, 13=C1->6, 14=R2->7, 15=C7->8, 16=C8->9). Only the resistor placement changed, so columns C2, C3 and C5 (pins 11, 10, A3) now carry a resistor and rows R1, R2, R4 (pins 2, 7, 5) do not.
Each column resistor has one leg in the Arduino header socket and the other twisted to a yellow jumper that goes to the matrix column pin.
Same parts as before: the parts list is unchanged; only wire labels were updated to match the new roles. The image shows pot1 (upper) wiper to A1 and pot2 (lower) wiper to A0.

The potentiometers go in neighbouring holes of one row (GND, SIG, VCC in columns 8-10 and 14-16, row c, top bank), per the catalogue card. Their wires use row a of the same column strips. The image draws the pots across the centre gap, but the electrical result is the same.
Breadboard power rails are the catalogue's tp (+) and tn (-) rails; the Arduino GND wire goes to GND.1. The potentiometers run on 5V.

graph_initial.title: 8x8 LED Matrix Row-Column Scanning
notes: Same parts as step 1, only labels changed: the circuit image shows pot1 (upper) wiper going to A1 and pot2 (lower) wiper going to A0, so pot1/pot2 and wire7/wire8 labels were corrected.

Matrix pin to Arduino pin follows the manual's pin table row by row, mapped to catalogue ports (matrix pin 1=R5, 2=R7, 3=C2, 4=C3, 5=R8, 6=C5, 7=R6, 8=R3, 9=R1, 10=C4, 11=C6, 12=R4, 13=C1, 14=R2, 15=C7, 16=C8).

The 8 x 1k resistors sit on the Arduino pins 2-9 wires, exactly as the image and table show. Those pins map to rows R1, R2, R4 and columns C1, C4, C6, C7, C8, so the resistors are on a mix of rows and columns. This is how the tutorial's image does it, so I followed it.
Each resistor has one leg in the Arduino header socket and the other twisted to a yellow jumper that goes to the matrix pin.

The potentiometers go in neighbouring holes of one row (GND, SIG, VCC in columns 8-10 and 14-16, row c, top bank), per the catalogue card. Their wires use row a of the same column strips. The image draws the pots across the centre gap, but the electrical result is the same.
Breadboard power rails are the catalogue's tp (+) and tn (-) rails. The image's rail strip is on the right side; the catalogue has a single rail pair.
The Arduino GND wire goes to GND.1 (the image shows one of the power-header GND pins). The potentiometers run on 5V.
